states.gapTheirs: The title bar says 'Untitled.md' rather than 'Untitled'. The '.md' adds a file-system suffix to the one line of chrome at the top, making the centred title about 157 px wide at device scale where B's is 111 px. states.verdict: The two frames are almost the same: a Library toggle, a centred name and a View button over empty paper, and a three-cell count at the foot. A spends its title on a file extension that a writer never needs to see on a blank page. B's bar is cleaner at the top, but at the foot its counts melt into one run of dark text, and your eye has to hunt for where each number ends. B is the room I'd rather sit in, but only just.

states.gap: The figures and labels share one grey (min ink #a2a2a2 on both), so a figure stands out from its label only by a weight step. At this dimmed strength the row reads as one flat 440 px strip. A uses two greys (#b6 figure, ~#d0 label) and its row is a tighter 408 px.
states.gapTheirs: The dimmed stats bar is too faint to read. Its labels ('words', 'characters', 'read') are about #d0d0d0 on #f9f9f9, a contrast of roughly 1.4:1, and its figures are only #b6b6b6. A glance at the word count while typing mostly shows the rule. B's single ink is about #a2a2a2 on #f7f7f7 and still reads.
states.verdict: With the title bar gone, both screens leave just the page and a whispered stats line on a hairline, which is the right amount of interface. In A the line has faded so far that checking the count while writing means leaning in and squinting at 'characters' before you find the number. B's line steps back just as far but you can still read it, and a semibold figure beside its regular label is enough to pick out '188'. B's row is a touch wider and a touch darker, which is a small price.

states.gap: Menu tick is a heavy filled ✔ glyph, about 2× the stroke of B's hairline ✓, and it reads darker than the label beside it. The panel is also ~335 display px wide against B's ~257 (about 1.3×), because the gap between the longest label and its chord is left loose.
states.gapTheirs: Row labels start at two different places. 'Enable Focus Mode', 'Hide Bars' and 'All Commands…' start ~23 device px left of 'Sentence', 'Dark Mode' and 'Statistics', which leaves a ragged left edge. The ticks also sit ~4 px below their labels' baseline, and the chords (Ctrl+D, Ctrl+Shift+H) ride ~2–3 px above the label baseline, so the key column doesn't line up with its rows.
states.verdict: B's View menu looks unaligned: its labels jump between two indents from row to row, and its ticks and key labels float off the baseline. That's the half-pixel sloppiness that makes a writer stop trusting the tool. A's menu is too wide and its check mark is too heavy, but every label, tick and chord lines up in clean columns with even 26 px rows. A's menu recedes and B's doesn't.

states.name: palette
states.gap: The chord labels at the right are set looser and hang lower than the command names beside them. 'Ctrl+D' spans ~72 device px in A against ~65 in B, about 10% wider. The '+' in 'Ctrl+=' and 'Ctrl+-' sits low against the letters. So the right-hand key column looks spaced out next to 24 px rows that are otherwise the same as B's (48 device px pitch on both).
states.gapTheirs: The palette's vertical rhythm is slightly off. The placeholder 'Search commands' sits ~3 device px above the middle of its ~84 px field (centre at y≈55 against the field's midline at ≈58), while A's is centred. Each small-caps heading also floats away from its own rows: 43 device px from the heading's baseline to its first row in B against 40 in A, with ~51 px above it on both sides. The headings read as loose dividers rather than labels that belong to the rows below.
states.verdict: Laid over each other, the two palettes are nearly the same: same panel width (~640 logical px), same 24 px rows, same #F2F2F2 panel grey, same accent-blue selected row with white type, same grey small caps. What separates them is spacing. A centres its search placeholder and keeps each section heading close to its rows. B lets the headings drift up and pushes the placeholder above the middle of the field. A's key-chord column is looser and lower-set than it should be, but that costs less than B's slack headings, so A takes it by a hair.
secondary: Both panels' bottom edges cut through a line of body text, leaving glyph fragments showing below the panel edge (A at the 'door took both hands' line, B at the 'She went down' line). Neither side ends the panel between lines.
Panel top sits at ~237 device px on both sides, about 13% of the way down the window. Neither is the third of the way down the spec calls for.
The selected row's fill is the same accent blue on both sides, 22 device px inset from each panel edge, with ~6 px corner radius. No difference.
The hairline under the search field and the panel shadow match within 1–2 px; A's shadow is marginally softer.
The palette fully covers the page's text behind it on both sides, with no bleed-through at #F2F2F2.
Stats bar under the palette: A sets figures and labels at one dark ink, B sets the figures in dark grey and the labels in a lighter grey. Per spec, that is a decision already taken, not a gap.
Title 'sample' vs 'Untitled.md', the gap above the first line, and the marker colour are excluded by spec and were not judged.

A's menu opens off to the lower right, away from the bar, like a context menu that landed in the wrong place. Even so, a menu in the right place with one wrong tick beats a correct menu in the wrong place.

states.gap: The selection fill on the page runs outside the text column. On the first line it goes about 125 px (display) past the line's end, out to x≈1693. states.gapTheirs: The foot uses two greys. Figures are about #444 and their labels a lighter grey of about #8a8a8a, so 'words', 'characters' and 'read' sit at roughly 3.4:1 on the #f9f9f9 paper. Against B's single dark ink the row goes faint while a selection is held, which is exactly when the writer is reading the counts. The title bar also shows the extension ('Untitled.md') where B shows the bare name, so 3 characters of file-system noise sit centred over the page.
states.verdict: B's foot reads like an instrument. Figure and word share one ink, and the figure is a weight step up, so 25 / 124 / < 1 min can be read at a glance without squinting at grey. A's foot fades into two greys when you most want the numbers, and its title bar carries a '.md' the writer never asked to see. B loses points for a selection block that spills past the measure like a spreadsheet highlight, but the bars themselves do the job better.
